h: Climb high, then cross the Humber
p: Not every child is born fearless, and that's absolutely fine. If yours is a bit wary of heights, let them start on the easiest wall and only go as high as they feel comfortable. Plenty of kids who freeze on the first attempt end the session racing to the top. Parents can help by cheering from the floor rather than pushing, and staff are always on hand to help with nerves. Wear something stretchy and leave jewellery at home.

Once your arms have recovered, there's plenty to do in and around Hull. East Park is a big, much-loved green space with a boating lake, play areas and an animal area, and it's a lovely spot for a picnic. Pickering Park on the west side of the city has a fishing lake and open space for a run-around.

Want to make a bigger trip of it? Drive west to the Humber Bridge and you can cross into North Lincolnshire, with the coast at Cleethorpes not far beyond for chips, sand and seaside amusements. Heading north instead, Beverley is a handsome market town with a magnificent minster and a racecourse on the Westwood common. If the coast is calling, Hornsea and Withernsea on the East Riding coast offer wide beaches and a breezier change of scene. Hull's Paragon Interchange brings trains and buses together, so the city is easy to reach without a car, and the city centre is compact enough to explore on foot.
